To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the OI-112 encoded nleB is a virulence factor that increases the pathogenicity of STEC strains; 2) low levels of mycotoxin contamination in feed can lead to STEC disease; 3) mycotox-ins alter STEC toxin expression; and, 4) a prebiotic/pro-biotic application alleviates the disease.
the STEC disease complex in calves is similar to that in mature cattle and that the OI-22 pathogenicity island is associated with the STECs eliciting serious disease.
mycotoxin mixtues are associated with Shigatoxin producing Escherichia col infections in dairy calves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of effective management strategies for the control and prevention of mycotoxin and STEC infections in calves.
the development of a novel approach to reduce the morbidity and mortalities associated with STEC infections in calves.
the development of a novel strategy for controlling STEC diseases in cattle and the prevention of human infections associated with the consumption of contaminated meat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mycotoxin contamination of feedstuffs is a significant factor in the development of disease in calves.

prebiotics and probiotics alleviate the morbidity and the mortality losses associated with STEC infections and that this is a result of their ability to eliminate the STEC and the mycotoxes that lead to disease.
mycotoxin exposure increases the virulence of STEC in dairy calves and that a prebiotic/probionic application alleviates disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mycotoxicosis and STEC complex in dairy calves is similar to that of the human disease.
prebiotic applications alleviate mycotoxin-induced pathogenesis.
the mycotoxicoses in cattle are not caused by mycotoxines but rather mycotoxin-producing fungi that interact with the commensal bacteria to cause disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mycotoxicoses are a significant disease problem that can be alleviated with prebiotic/probiotic applications.
the same STEC virulence genes and toxin activity mechanisms exist in calves and mature cattle.
mycotoxin exposure in calves is associated with serious disease.
